claim: Found the real, live-writable render source for Moonlight Syndrome's dialogue text: a small 2-byte 'glyph cache coordinate' field inside each character's GPU sprite-primitive entry (the repeating 4-word structure documented earlier this investigation). Writing a different, already-cached glyph's coordinate into this field changes the on-screen character CLEANLY -- no garbling, no position/width corruption -- confirmed twice independently on two different characters in the same line.
context: Follows directly from the prior correction (evidence/moonlight_syndrome_clean_retest_no_effect/): the decompressed script buffer at RAM pointer 0x801e84a4 is confirmed NOT to drive rendering. Using the new save-state slot-1 checkpoint (evidence/moonlight_syndrome_savestate_slot1_checkpoint/) for fast iteration, tried the GPU-primitive list directly instead -- the layer closest to actual pixels, one level past the script buffer.
method: Loaded save-state slot 1 (the frozen pre-display checkpoint), let the dialogue line render naturally and completely unpatched.

Read the live GPU-primitive list for the rendered line's first two characters at 0x8008f640 -- each character's entry is 4 words: [X-advance + line-bank], [constant 0x7e808080 command/tint tag], [destination-slot counter], [glyph-cache coordinate + constant 0xc07f tag].

Entry 1 (originally the character '・', a middle dot) had glyph-coordinate bytes 30 00. Overwrote both the front-buffer copy (0x8008f64c) and its double-buffer twin 0x1000 bytes later (0x9064c) with bytes d0 70 -- a coordinate already observed elsewhere in this investigation as producing the character 'ん' (n).
Screenshot confirmed: the first character changed cleanly from '・' to 'ん' -- the line read 'ん・・あんなのだったら' instead of the original '・・・あんなのだったら'.
Repeated on entry 2 (the second middle dot): overwrote both buffer copies (0x8008f65c and 0x9065c) with bytes 40 60 -- a coordinate observed elsewhere as producing 'な' (na).
Screenshot confirmed: the second character also changed cleanly, to 'な' -- the line then read 'んな あんなのだったら'.
result: Two independent, clean, non-garbled character substitutions in the same real dialogue line, both confirmed by screenshot. This is the actual, live, writable text-rendering source for this game -- not the script buffer this investigation spent most of its effort on, but a specific 2-byte field inside each character's own GPU sprite-primitive command.

important_caveats: This proves WRITABILITY at the GPU-primitive layer using coordinates for glyphs already known from earlier observation in this same investigation -- it has NOT yet been tried with a coordinate for a glyph never seen live before, so the full (column,row)-to-character atlas map is still only partially known (limited to characters this investigation happened to observe by chance).

Both buffer copies (front and back, 0x1000 apart) had to be patched for the change to hold reliably across the double-buffered render -- patching only one copy earlier in this pass produced no visible change, consistent with the emulator flipping between the two.

This was done live, in RAM, during active emulation -- not yet built into a repeatable tool or a disc-level patch. Turning this into an actual translation-injection pipeline (mapping every needed character to its atlas coordinate, and writing the GPU-primitive commands for a whole replacement sentence, ideally from a static disc/resource edit rather than a live RAM poke) is real, separate, scoped follow-up work.
